Maestro

The Workshop Notebook. A warm-paper workbench for reading, judging and correcting the design of a game. Every token, every named rule and every shared component, rendered by the system itself.

Text Input

Named rules

  • The Two Exemptions Rule. The chrome is achromatic. Exactly two chromatic tokens exist outside the data palette, accent and danger, and a third is admitted only against this test: not 'would a colour help' but 'is there a fact on screen that nothing else says'.
  • The Ink Button Rule. The primary button is ink on paper. A button filled with the accent is forbidden.
  • The Two Grounds Rule. ground is darker than paper on purpose. The diagram lies on the desk; the reading panels are sheets on top of it.
  • The Two Voices Rule. The tool speaks sans, the game speaks serif. If it would survive the game shipping, it is serif.
  • The No Uppercase Rule. Labels are sentence case with light tracking. All-caps labels are the admin-panel tell.
  • The Copyable Is Mono Rule. If a value is a machine identifier a person might paste, it is monospace.
  • The Warm Shadow Rule. Every shadow is rgba(94, 72, 55, ...), the paper's own brown. Pure black is forbidden everywhere.
  • The Earned Elevation Rule. A shadow answers a question about stacking, never about importance.
  • The Named Absence Rule. Nothing is blank because a value is missing. Absent gets a word, empty gets a different word.

Do and don't

Do

  • Do set every game-owned word in Literata and every tool-owned word in Fira Sans.
  • Do keep rows at 36px and lists dense.
  • Do tint every shadow with rgba(94, 72, 55, ...).
  • Do name absences in words: 'no zone', 'never reviewed', 'no requirement'.
  • Do state read-only where the missing action would be.
  • Do mark the current item with weight and aria-current.
  • Do cap prose at 68ch.
  • Do build every repeated pattern once, as a shared component.

Don't

  • Don't build the generic admin panel: no icon sidebar, no card grid of counters.
  • Don't reach for the dark blue SaaS dashboard.
  • Don't borrow GitHub's chrome.
  • Don't bury content the way the ad-choked game wiki does.
  • Don't produce the empty beautiful landing page.
  • Don't use #000 or #fff anywhere, including in a shadow.
  • Don't fill a button, a badge or a header with the accent.
  • Don't use border-left or border-right above 1px as a coloured stripe.
  • Don't set a label in all caps.
  • Don't nest a panel inside a panel.
  • Don't leave a cell blank when the value is absent.
  • Don't animate layout properties, and never use bounce or elastic easing.
  • Don't add a modal before an inline alternative has been ruled out in writing.
